Net Income vs Free Cash Flow vs Owner FCF
charts.annotation: Owner FCF, where shown, is the DCF's series after SBC, interest income and lease principal.

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Shougang Fushan Resources Group Limited: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Shougang Fushan Resources Group Limited: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For Shougang Fushan Resources Group Limited: read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Shougang Fushan Resources Group Limited: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Shougang Fushan Resources Group Limited: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Shougang Fushan Resources Group Limited: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Shougang Fushan Resources Group Limited: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Shougang Fushan Resources Group Limited: NetIncome here is the owners' share only. The Liulin mine subsidiaries carry minority interests (~11% of equity), and the NCI's cut of profit is a real leakage the DCF charges explicitly: FY2025 dividends paid out to minority shareholders (HK$709m, per the kpis table) exceeded owners' NetIncome (HK$632m) that year. Total profit including NCI was HK$745m in FY2025 versus owners' HK$632m -- the gap is cash the group earned but that isn't available to Shougang Fushan's own shareholders.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)
  • NCI dividends spiking in a weak owners'-profit year (FY2025)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Shougang Fushan Resources Group Limited: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Shougang Fushan Resources Group Limited: SBC is nil here -- the step in shares outstanding (4,926.8m to 5,091.1m between FY2023 and FY2024) is not dilution but a one-off rights issue that raised HK$425.5m. Per-share figures (EPS, DPS) before FY2024 are not directly comparable to after without adjusting for the enlarged share base.

What to watch:

  • No further step changes expected -- the rights issue was a single event, not an ongoing dilution pattern
  • EPS growth measured off the post-rights-issue share count

dcf.base_sublabel: Owner FCF — after SBC, interest income & leases
dcf.model_approach_note: WACC premium +2.5pt (10.0%->12.5% all scenarios): +1.0pt extreme cyclicality (FY2022 EBITDA HK$5,106m vs FY2025 HK$1,451m, 3.5x peak-to-trough), +1.0pt regulatory single point of failure (mining licenses 7-17yr, reserves on unrevised 2007 estimate), +0.5pt geographic concentration (all 3 mines in Liulin, Shanxi; all sales in China). Customer-concentration and small-cap-illiquidity premiums not applied (Shougang Group 14-39% of revenue, below the 40% trigger; market cap ~US$1.8bn, above the $300m small-cap trigger). Exit-multiple cap (#4) not stacked on top -- the ~9yr reserve-life taper already caps terminal value at 1x base/4x bull EV/EBITDA, both within the 10yr historical range.
